title: Replace per-command pkexec with privileged D-Bus control
description: Add a dedicated root LegionControl1 system-bus service with session-scoped Polkit authorization, a typed allow-listed hardware/service API, and a Flutter client that replaces repeated pkexec legion_cli and pkexec systemctl launches. Keep LegionTelemetry1 read-only and separately sandboxed.
acceptance_criteria: The first privileged frontend action authenticates once through Polkit; subsequent allowed actions on the same D-Bus connection do not reprompt; authorization is revoked on disconnect; arbitrary commands, paths, units, and unsupported values are rejected; telemetry remains read-only; backend, Flutter, service, and NixOS tests/builds pass.
notes:
Implemented LegionControl1 root system-bus service, sender-scoped Polkit authorization, strict typed allow-lists, bounded payload/output handling, timeout/disconnect cleanup, Flutter D-Bus client migration with no pkexec fallback, NixOS/systemd/D-Bus/Polkit packaging, diagnostics/recovery copy, and fail-closed UI for unsupported mutations. Verified 493 Flutter tests, flutter analyze, Linux release build, Nix service package CTest/build, and standalone NixOS module evaluation. Runtime Polkit prompt reuse and disconnect revocation still require deployment from a privileged shell.
Deployment configuration committed and pushed in nixos-flaky-tests at 4ed6366, pinning frontend 479aeb5 and backend c539a86 and enabling services.legionControl. Full dirty-tree NixOS toplevel build passed. Installation remains blocked in this execution environment because sudo is denied by no_new_privileges; keep issue in_progress until live Polkit prompt reuse/disconnect revocation are verified.
Live test confirmed one Polkit authorization prompt, but legion_cli failed because the NixOS system service PATH omitted bash. Fix adds immutable bashNonInteractive, e2fsprogs, and util-linux paths; NixOS supplies baseline coreutils/grep/systemd paths. Standalone module evaluation asserts all added runtime packages and the service package build passes.

title: Validate M1CN Custom mode after WMI setter fix

Capture platform_profile, powermode, thermalmode, AC state, and focused kernel logs before testing power-limit writes.
acceptance_criteria: On AC power, selecting Custom succeeds; platform_profile reads custom; raw powermode reads 255; thermalmode reads 3; no WMI evaluation error or duplicate write occurs.
notes:
Upstream integration and Nix validation completed: c539a86 is the validated three-commit fork tip atop upstream 3893e20, and the Linux 7.2.1 module plus full NixOS toplevel build succeeded. Runtime acceptance remains pending reboot.
Automated boot-generation installation was attempted but blocked before any system change because this execution environment sets no_new_privs and cannot run sudo. Run sudo nixos-rebuild boot --flake /home/prnice/Dotfiles/nixos-flaky-tests#nixos from a normal privileged shell, then reboot.

title: Validate and deploy iGPU-only graphics modes
description: Deploy LenovoLegionLinux main c539a8637eb8f39a0aafe69241f921d6cc116e13 (graphics port 13dd1bf) on the Legion Slim 7 16APH8, perform the controlled Hybrid to Hybrid iGPU-only and Auto hardware matrix, prove BIOS rollback, then enable the firmware-advertised modes in the Flutter frontend.
acceptance_criteria: Hardened driver and combined graphics-mode CLI are deployed; Hybrid iGPU-only and Auto are validated across PCI/DRM topology, internal and external displays, Wayland session survival, suspend/resume, AC/battery transitions, reboot persistence, and BIOS rollback; Flutter consumes status/choices and enables only advertised modes with tests.
notes: The original graphics commit 5a2a2d1 was ported onto current upstream as 13dd1bf and is included in fork main c539a86. Python tests, CLI smoke test, checkpatch, kernel module build, and full NixOS toplevel build passed; disruptive hardware validation remains pending reboot.

title: Investigate iGPU-only graphics mode in legion driver
description: Determine whether the Legion Slim 7 16APH8 M1CN firmware and LenovoLegionLinux driver can safely expose a true integrated-only graphics mode distinct from Hybrid runtime suspend and Discrete-only mode. Define and implement an authoritative read/write capability only if verified.
acceptance_criteria: Read-only firmware and driver evidence identifies whether integrated-only exists; any API exposes enum mode and choices with authoritative readback and unsupported states; write behavior is safe, reboot-aware, and validated across display routing, suspend/resume, and rollback; frontend integration requirements are recorded.
notes: Firmware investigation completed against M1CN48WW DSDT: support values 3/2 are positive capability codes, iGPU selector values map Default/IGPUOnly/Auto, and gsync plus igpumode form Hybrid/Hybrid iGPU-only/Hybrid Auto/Discrete. Driver commit 5a2a2d1 adds capability-gated visibility, bounded and serialized WMI writes, strict readback, transactional combined CLI transitions with verified rollback, synthetic platform path discovery, and five focused tests. Nix kernel module and Python package builds pass; live read-only CLI reports hybrid and all four choices. No iGPU-mode write was attempted. Deployment and controlled hardware validation remain tracked in lllf-j9t.
close_reason: Firmware semantics and hardened kernel/CLI contract completed in driver commit 5a2a2d1; deployment, disruptive hardware validation, and Flutter enablement split to lllf-j9t.

title: Expose graphics modes and hand off iGPU-only support

acceptance_criteria: The dGPU page clearly presents Hybrid, Integrated only, and Discrete only; only backend-supported modes are actionable; reboot and display-routing consequences are clear; overclock is separate; compact/wide tests and quality gates pass; the driver handoff gives another agent concrete discovery, implementation, and safety steps.

Battery reports unavailable temperature truthfully, identifies power_now as battery-side charge/discharge power, uses semantic green native controls, removes duplicate title and bottom refresh, and improves chart interaction. dGPU matches Section 09 hierarchy without duplicate title and remains responsive/safe. Tests, analyzer, detector, and release build pass.

title: Make dGPU deactivation baselines atomic in backend
description: Extend legion_cli dGPU commands so the privileged backend receives and validates the expected PID set and PCI address immediately before acting. The frontend now rechecks baselines before invocation, but kill-processes still kills whichever processes exist when the backend runs, leaving a TOCTOU race and PID-reuse risk.
acceptance_criteria: kill-processes accepts an expected process baseline and refuses changed targets; restart-pci accepts an expected PCI address and refuses active compute processes or a changed target; frontend passes the baseline; race/safety behavior is covered by backend and frontend tests.

acceptance_criteria: Sidebar battery icon uses the redesign's green semantic color; discharging shows estimated time left; charging shows estimated time to full; invalid or unavailable telemetry omits estimates; light detail background, sidebar, card fill, and card borders match the redesign; compact/wide tests and quality gates pass.

title: Harden fan and power telemetry UI

acceptance_criteria: Invalid fan curve data renders a truthful unavailable state instead of a collapsed graph; live package/GPU draw replaces misleading 0 W limit facts; fan units and max RPM are correct; fan and overclock toggles use the dashboard pattern; precise controls match the current visual system; compact and wide tests plus full quality gates pass.

title: Polish power profile ownership UI
Integrate power profiles daemon with Power controls
description: Route standard power profiles through power-profiles-daemon so amd-pstate and platform_profile remain synchronized, retain Lenovo-only Extreme and Custom modes, use the Yaru-native selector, and add truthful AC/custom staging affordances where backend support exists.
design: Use a dedicated unprivileged PPD D-Bus service. PPD owns standard profile writes; direct Legion profile writes remain only for firmware profiles PPD cannot represent. Do not expose duplicate amd-pstate writers.
acceptance_criteria: Standard Quiet/Balanced/Performance writes use PPD when available; Lenovo-only modes remain explicit; the selector is Yaru-native and responsive; power-limit staging cannot apply outside supported prerequisites; automated tests and Linux quality gates pass.
notes: Implemented shared PPD D-Bus coordination for Power and Dashboard. Standard profiles use org.freedesktop.UPower.PowerProfiles; vendor Custom/Extreme pair with PPD performance and use the Legion direct writer. Firmware choices are validated before PPD mutation, and returning from unrecognized vendor profiles repairs PPD no-ops. Power UI uses YaruChoiceChipBar, displays daemon/driver and AC state, stages limit edits behind Custom+AC, and rolls back earlier batch writes on later failure. Verified against live PPD 0.30 properties. Quality gates: 421 tests, flutter analyze, Impeccable detector, Linux release build.
close_reason: PPD integration, Yaru selector, staged guarded limits, rollback, tests, and documentation completed.

title: Deploy Kernel 7 Legion fan driver
description: Replace the active pre-Kernel-7 LenovoLegionLinux read_file_fix pin with a tested immutable revision containing upstream PRs #423 and #434, rebuild and reboot NixOS, then verify the synthetic legion platform device and legion_hwmon on Lenovo 82Y4 / M1CN48WW. Preserve existing dirty NixOS configuration changes. Exact evidence and safe procedure are in docs/architecture/fan-controller-kernel-7-handoff.md.
acceptance_criteria: NixOS source pin contains upstream merges 1570dba2c8c3079115439f43e50d2891813c38d9 and c52b4f293c4e8c00acf6bfba2bbd06b862cdf4a1; rebuilt generation boots; PNP0C09 remains owned by acpi-ec; synthetic platform:legion/legion binds; kernel logs show successful probe; legion_hwmon exposes truthful fan limits and curve points; frontend reads the real curve; results are recorded without unsafe live EC rebinding.
notes:
Phase 0 read-only /dev/mem capture decoded (2026-08-30, balanced, AC): DFAN+0xF0 power limits are live and match DSDT defaults exactly; the DFAN curve area and step indices are all zero on a clean boot, and F10A==0 means GFAN returns the ACPI CFST package initializer (1..8,8,8) verbatim - the exported curve is a DSDT constant, not hardware state. Revised fix: compose the curve from the A7/SFTW per-mode FACT tables (RPM palette + CPU temps + max speeds) plus step indices; writes via Fan_Set_Table (mode + ten step indices), then verify the populated DFAN registers read-only as the round-trip check. Updated plan and evidence in docs/architecture/legion-driver-issues-handoff.md.
Phase 1 built 2026-08-30: driver main bafa1f3 restores kernel_module exactly from deployed Kernel-7 upstream 3893e20 and retires read_file_fix; f4849cd selects M1CN ACCESS_METHOD_WMI3 power limits, probes/hides unsupported and legacy-only WMI3 fields, gates writes to Custom mode, and demotes legacy raw-value polling to pr_debug. NixOS toplevel build succeeded; module store path 79yjssydl0q1hfs4v9ggkfrsk7lmk9fl has vermagic 7.2.0 and contains the new rejection path. Boot validation pending. Global NO_ACCESS hiding was not used because many older models rely on that historical legacy fallback.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Phase 1 reboot validation passed 2026-08-30. Booted module resolves to the expected 79yjssyd store path on kernel 7.2.0; synthetic legion device bound successfully. In low-power on battery, supported WMI3 power fields read 54/54/65/45 W CPU, 100 C CPU, 60 W cTGP, 87 C GPU, and 45 W target offset, stable across three passes. Unsupported and legacy-only fields are hidden; raw-value log spam is absent; 38 focused frontend power tests pass. No writes were attempted. Fan-curve implementation and Custom+AC write/read-back/rollback validation remain open.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Live frontend visual validation passed: Power displays CPU sustained/boost/peak/cross-load 54/54/65/45 W and GPU total/temperature 60 W/87 C, matching sysfs, and correctly disables editing while ACAD reports offline.

title: Define authoritative power-limit defaults
description: The Power page now stages and reverts edits to the live controller baseline, but Restore defaults cannot be implemented truthfully because the Legion backend exposes writable current limits without a complete authoritative default set. Determine whether firmware, a model database, or an upstream CLI command can provide per-model defaults, then expose Restore defaults only when that source is available.
design: Do not infer defaults from slider bounds or label CPUDefaultPowerLimit as a complete preset. Reuse the staged batch and rollback path once trustworthy values exist.
acceptance_criteria: A documented authoritative source supplies defaults for every exposed limit; unsupported models do not show a restore action; restoring is AC/Custom gated, confirmed, rollback-safe, and tested.
notes: Candidate default source found 2026-08-30 in the M1CN48WW DSDT: WMAE GetFeatureValue lazily initializes EC defaults (CPU short 54W, long 54W, peak 65W, cross-load 45W, CPU temp 100C, GPU PPAB 20W, cTGP 60W, GPU temp 87C), and the A7/SFTW WMI data block exposes per-mode fan tables with CurrentFanMaxSpeed/DefaultFanMaxSpeed. Verify against a second capture before exposing a restore action; APU SPPT and CPU L1 tau are unsupported on this firmware and must stay hidden.

comments.author: Prn-Ice
comments.text: Second immutable-boot read capture confirms stable current/default-like values for all exposed fields: CPU 54/54/65/45 W and 100 C; GPU cTGP 60 W and 87 C. GPU PPAB remains hidden because live WMI3 reports 0 despite the DSDT lazy-init candidate of 20 W. Keep Restore defaults unavailable until that discrepancy and a complete authoritative exposed-field preset are resolved.
